one_line: A caregiver-focused patient portal where agents coordinate care inside the signed-in session.
what_it_does: Handles appointments, medications, results, and messages across a proxy-access patient portal, with confirmation gates for consequential writes.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools and shared signed-in state make cross-module caregiver work materially more reliable than an agent clicking a conventional portal; confirmation boundaries preserve human control.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes four cross-module WebMCP workflows in an authenticated session.
Frame sheets show medical portal sections, records, messages, and appointment/form states.
Tools are intentionally absent for signing consent or changing proxy permissions.
execution_rationale: The product surface is coherent and unusually well scoped, with a visible portal workflow and explicit read/confirm/not-exposed state handling; end-to-end detail is limited by the lack of transcript.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion sheets show portal navigation and populated care views.
Description specifies realistic seed data and confirmation cards with editable drafts.
Devpost packaging and frames agree on the caregiver portal workflow.
impact_rationale: Caregivers have a concrete, high-friction problem and the product directly reduces the work while respecting sensitive-care authorization.
impact_evidence: Description identifies fragmented caregiver tasks across appointments, medications, results, and messages.
Proxy access and human approval address a credible healthcare use case.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native shared state and graduated authorization to family healthcare is a thoughtful, memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent follows the user’s active family-member context while the page highlights each tool target.
Consent/signature boundaries are part of the product concept rather than an afterthought.
usability_note: Clear modules and approval gates; healthcare portal complexity remains inherently high.

one_line: A source-backed municipal planning evidence desk for people and browser agents.
what_it_does: Searches, inspects, and stages filing-level planning evidence into a dated brief for human review.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, change listing, inspection, and staging preserve filing identity and provenance more reliably than generic browsing across fragmented civic records.
leverage_evidence: Description reports four distinct WebMCP calls completed in one visible workflow.
Frames show source cards, evidence panels, and organized report blocks.
Human review is required before anything is published or sent.
execution_rationale: The central evidence-to-brief workflow appears coherent and intentionally handles changed outcomes and multiple filings, though the visual text is only partly legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a multi-step civic research workflow and assembled evidence views.
Packet names distinct records and a three-filing brief staged for review.
Packaging matches the source-backed planning-desk concept.
impact_rationale: Land and development professionals, journalists, lenders, and planners have a real need to detect quiet procedural changes in public records.
impact_evidence: Description gives a concrete Bentonville/Rogers planning-record problem.
Filing-level distinctions address a documented failure mode of agenda-only heuristics.
creativity_rationale: The evidence handoff between a researcher and an agent, centered on procedural truth rather than generic summarization, is a fresh civic-research interaction.
creativity_evidence: Product focuses on living filing-level evidence and dated changes.
Shared human/agent review surface is central to the concept.
usability_note: Evidence-first workflow is legible, though civic-record complexity may require onboarding.
advance_reason: Strong niche impact and credible structured-evidence workflow.

one_line: An auditable decision workspace that turns vendor proposals into shared evidence and scenarios.
what_it_does: Builds criteria, requirements, cost models, risks, evidence links, scenarios, rankings, and a human-approved decision record.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes the semantics of a decision model rather than merely UI controls, enabling precise agent construction and inspectable shared state.
leverage_evidence: Description lists structured tools for criteria, requirements, claims, risks, TCO, scenarios, and review.
Frames show comparison, evidence, and recommendation-style panels.
Human approval is the final gate.
execution_rationale: The surfaces form a coherent procurement decision workflow with multiple analytical views; the packet does not fully prove every listed capability.
execution_evidence: Product-motion sheets show document inputs, normalized comparison views, and decision panels.
Description specifies evidence matrix, cost, risk, scenario, and audit timeline views.
impact_rationale: Procurement teams face exactly the fragmented, high-stakes comparison problem addressed by an auditable decision model.
impact_evidence: Vendor proposal comparison is a concrete business use case.
Inspectable assumptions and evidence improve reviewability of recommendations.
creativity_rationale: Reframing an agent from summarizer into a co-builder of an auditable decision system is an original and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: WebMCP is used to construct decision semantics, not just navigate forms.
Scenario testing and evidence-linked claims are pursued as one workspace.
usability_note: Rich model supports serious review but could be demanding for first-time users.
standouts: Decision provenance is treated as a first-class UI object.
advance_reason: Strong agent-native decision workflow with credible business value.

one_line: A private in-browser CSV analysis workbench whose agent receives answers rather than raw rows.
what_it_does: Loads and analyzes sensitive CSVs locally, exposing dataset description, aggregation, filtering, trends, anomaly, and expense tools.
leverage_rationale: In-page tools let an agent analyze private live state without exfiltrating rows; this privacy and precision boundary is materially better than UI-driving or uploading data.
leverage_evidence: Description states parsing and analysis stay inside the browser tab.
Seven tools return answers while rows are highlighted locally.
Packet claims empty network activity during conversation.
execution_rationale: The workbench has a focused workflow and concrete analytic outputs, visibly supported by dark data/tool panels; the agent-to-result sequence is not fully readable.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show data workbench states, tool/configuration surfaces, and processed outputs.
Description specifies 965 synthetic transactions, 12 categories, and anomaly detection.
impact_rationale: People and small teams have a real need to analyze financial or payroll-like CSVs without sending raw records to an external service.
impact_evidence: Privacy-preserving local analysis addresses a concrete barrier to using AI on sensitive data.
Use cases include spending and payslip analysis.
creativity_rationale: The answer-only agent surface plus local row highlighting is a compelling privacy-first interaction design.
creativity_evidence: Shared page state supports both machine aggregates and human-readable highlighted rows.
No-backend architecture is aligned with the core premise.
usability_note: Focused tool set and visual highlights support comprehension; CSV schema constraints may limit novices.
standouts: Privacy receipt and answer-only architecture make WebMCP consequential.
advance_reason: Strong privacy and structured-analysis delta with concrete execution evidence.

one_line: A dependency watch that diffs agent-stack APIs and MCP servers for production teams.
what_it_does: Tracks manifests, tools, schemas, changelogs, and deprecations, classifies changes, and checks a pasted MCP configuration.
leverage_rationale: Conversational dependency queries and identical human/agent actions in one logged page are useful, though a conventional API or dashboard could provide much of the same value.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies six WebMCP tools and a shared HUMAN/AGENT log.
Frames show dependency/audit panels and report-like findings.
check_dependencies returns matched and breaking dependencies.
execution_rationale: The product is coherent, with a clear watch-diff-audit workflow and concrete dependency findings; some claimed breadth is packaging evidence rather than fully observed.
execution_evidence: Motion sheets show audit configuration and results views.
Packet reports 48 servers, 119 URLs, classifications, and line-level diffs.
impact_rationale: Production agent teams have a real operational risk in silently changing MCP and model dependencies, and the product gives them actionable diffs.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and dependency-monitoring problem are clearly articulated.
Breaking-change classification and saved dependency lists fit the workflow.
creativity_rationale: The agent-stack dependency-watch concept is a fresh application of WebMCP, though it extends familiar dependency monitoring patterns.
creativity_evidence: Same-page human and agent audit trail is a notable interaction detail.
Coverage spans MCP servers and major model APIs.
usability_note: Audit-oriented information architecture appears clear, with useful filtering.
standouts: Strong operational framing for agent reliability.
advance_reason: Credible developer audience and well-defined monitoring workflow.

one_line: A persistent 3D MMO where an agent observes and operates the human player’s live session.
what_it_does: Exposes tools for world observation, inventory, movement, targeting, and interaction in a shared persistent simulation.
leverage_rationale: Structured world state and action tools are central to reliable agent participation in a live game; pixel-oriented browser driving cannot replicate this comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Pitch lists six native tools for observation, inventory, movement, targeting, and activation.
Frame sheets consistently show a live 3D game world and changed/overlaid states.
Human and agent share one operator session and persistent state.
execution_rationale: The game client and shared-world concept are visibly real and coherent, but the packet identifies it as a prototype and the exact complete gameplay loop is only partly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show a consistent top-down 3D world with controls and state changes.
Description specifies an existing persistent simulation and concrete interaction tools.
impact_rationale: It offers meaningful entertainment and experimentation value for players interested in AI-native persistent worlds, though the audience and prototype maturity are narrower.
impact_evidence: Persistent MMO gameplay and human-agent coexistence are a clear entertainment use case.
Frames show playable world presentation rather than a static mockup.
creativity_rationale: A persistent MMO with an agent operating the same human avatar/world is an unusually memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Shared operator session avoids creating a separate AI world.
World observation and action are exposed as native game semantics.
usability_note: Game controls appear coherent; agent-assisted play and prototype status may create onboarding friction.
red_flags: Description says Tartarian existed before the challenge; WebMCP addition is the likely new contribution.
standouts: Most ambitious shared-world agent interaction in the packet.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP fit and exceptional concept ambition.

one_line: An intent-driven storefront that composes a purpose-built shopping experience on arrival.
what_it_does: Takes a shopper’s intent, streams a branded storefront as layout patches, and recomposes it as the shopper narrows requirements.
leverage_rationale: The product’s defining behavior is agent intent becoming the page itself, not merely an agent searching a fixed UI; that is a substantial WebMCP-driven change in the commerce interaction.
leverage_evidence: Description says storefronts are composed from intent over navigator.modelContext.
Frame sheets show commerce listings, product detail, prices, and selected results.
RFC 6902 patches update a live layout tree across turns.
execution_rationale: The visual storefront flow is coherent and demonstrates product/catalog states, but the packet gives limited proof of the underlying streaming and multi-turn recomposition beyond the claim.
execution_evidence: Motion sheets show shopping results and detail states.
Description specifies intent, catalog composition, branded layout, and narrowing behavior.
impact_rationale: Shoppers and merchants have a clear value proposition: less irrelevant browsing and more direct matching to constraints such as fit, price, and shipping.
impact_evidence: Concrete shopping intent example includes wide fit, budget, and delivery date.
Purpose-built storefront reduces the search burden of fixed catalog pages.
creativity_rationale: The idea that a store is generated for each agent intent, then disappears, is a genuinely novel commerce interaction pursued at ambitious architectural depth.
creativity_evidence: Intent-first storefront composition challenges the fixed-page assumption.
Live layout-tree patching is a distinctive implementation model.
usability_note: Intent-first results can be efficient, while merchant/catalog coverage is a likely practical constraint.
standouts: Strongest conceptual rethinking of the website surface.
advance_reason: Highly original agent-native commerce model with visible storefront execution.

one_line: An adaptive handwriting coach that analyzes children’s strokes and guides remediation.
what_it_does: Offers traced and freehand practice for letters, numbers, and shapes, with stroke analytics, feedback, progress, rewards, and WebMCP devtools.
leverage_rationale: Agents can receive structured stroke analytics and adapt exercises in a shared learning state, beyond what generic UI clicking can reliably coordinate.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies real-time stroke analysis and an adaptive remediation loop.
Frames show handwriting practice screens, feedback/assessment states, and analytics styling.
Packet lists eight registered tools and learner progress surfaces.
execution_rationale: The product has an unusually broad but coherent educational surface, and the motion sheets show practice and feedback states; exact closed-loop behavior is only partly visible.
execution_evidence: Thirteen gallery images are reported and three video sheets show practice/feedback progression.
Description enumerates dashboard, analytics, rewards, profiles, and devtools.
Packaging and frames agree on a polished handwriting-coach workflow.
impact_rationale: Children learning handwriting and the parents/teachers supporting them are a specific audience with a real need for stroke-order and motor-habit feedback.
impact_evidence: Problem distinguishes pixel overlap from direction and stroke behavior.
Adaptive coaching addresses limited adult one-on-one time.
creativity_rationale: Combining fine-motor stroke semantics, autonomous coaching, and adaptive remediation is a strong, memorable educational interaction.
creativity_evidence: Five-dimensional stroke evaluation and remediation loop go beyond static worksheet checking.
Multiple practice modes connect assessment to muscle-memory learning.
usability_note: Modes and gamification support engagement; the breadth may require careful learner onboarding.
standouts: Concrete educational value grounded in stroke-level behavior.
advance_reason: High-impact learning use case with substantial product depth.

one_line: A shared garden canvas where agents design beds under horticultural rules and humans review the result.
what_it_does: Manages two garden beds, crop catalog, care calendar, and plant diagnosis through validated, logged WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured garden state and deterministic validation let the agent negotiate real constraints on the same visible canvas, substantially more reliably than clicking cells.
leverage_evidence: Description lists six tools including design, suggest, diagnose, state, and task logging.
Frame sheets show garden/grid layouts and updated plant/configuration panels.
Rules engine is shared by UI and tools and validates every action.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and coherent, with visible beds, care tasks, diagnosis, and activity logging; the product appears complete for a hackathon garden planner.
execution_evidence: Motion sheets show completed grid layouts and configuration states.
Packet specifies 27 plants, two beds, calendar, doctor, and activity panel.
Pure testable horticultural engine is the single source of truth.
impact_rationale: Home and urban gardeners have a real planning and plant-care need; the niche value is credible even though the domain is recreational.
impact_evidence: Companion planting, spacing, sun, and season constraints are concrete gardening problems.
Care calendar and diagnosis address ongoing use, not just one layout.
creativity_rationale: Garden planning is a fresh domain for structured human-agent collaboration, and the rules-pushback interaction is playful and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Agent drafts while deterministic horticultural rules push back.
Shared canvas makes agent actions visible and consequential.
usability_note: Visible validation and activity log make collaboration understandable for gardeners.
standouts: Excellent category-neutral demonstration of rules-aware collaboration.
advance_reason: Clear shared-state product with strong validation and an engaging niche use case.

one_line: A local data-cleaning workbench where agents propose diffs and people approve every write.
what_it_does: Profiles, queries, charts, and cleans messy CSVs entirely in-browser, presenting exact before/after proposals for approval.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on the same private data object as the human while exposing safe read tools and diff-only writes; generic UI automation cannot provide the same reliable privacy and approval semantics.
leverage_evidence: Description states one shared JavaScript store for UI and tools.
Every write is an exact before/after diff requiring human approval; no mutation tool is exposed.
Frame sheets show spreadsheet-like tables, highlighted changes, and cleanup/result states.
execution_rationale: The workflow is exceptionally coherent for its scope: inspect, identify, propose, review, approve/reject, with visible data states and a clear privacy boundary.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show tabular workbench states and changed/highlighted cells.
Description specifies profiling, querying, charting, proposals, approval cards, and zero-data-upload premise.
Rules for reads and writes are consistent across the product description and visuals.
impact_rationale: Analysts regularly face messy sensitive CSVs, and this directly addresses both the cleanup burden and the compliance/privacy barrier to AI assistance.
impact_evidence: Concrete problems include inconsistent regions, currency/date formats, and duplicates.
Local processing is suited to customer, salary, and other sensitive records.
creativity_rationale: The strict proposal-not-mutation contract and privacy receipt turn data cleaning into a well-designed human-agent control model.
creativity_evidence: Undo is deliberately human-owned while agent writes are approval-gated diffs.
The agent gets tools, not raw data, while the human sees the exact consequences.
usability_note: Diff cards, highlights, and explicit approval make risky transformations understandable.
standouts: Best safety and privacy contract in the set.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, execution, and concrete analyst impact.
